This is a common interpretation of virtual particles, but not entirely accurate.

The universe appears to be run by probability waves. They move like ripples on a pond, and the size of the wave at a given location tells how likely we are to find a particle there.

Particles can transform from one type into another, and these new particles have probability waves too. When you add up the probabilities, it turns out that the waves of most new particles tend to cancel out as time goes by. Some people describe this as a temporary particle popping into and out of existence, but this is not correct. A virtual particle is actually the influence of what might have happened on what actually did happen. Virtual particles are bookkeeping tools to tally up all the possible histories of a system.

In the case of the EM Drive, it is completely wrong. If the EmDrive actually works, virtual particles do not explain it. The virtual particles are invisible internal parts of the process. If it is producing thrust, it must be emitting real particles that carry away the missing momentum. What those particles are is anybody's guess.
